findings.title: Cleanup interval reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute
findings.body: This PR changes the global cleanup ticker from 10 minutes to 1 minute. The cleanup loop runs every cleanup job, including temporary file cleanup, snapshot deletion, dashboard-version deletion, image cleanup, short URL cleanup, query-history cleanup, and annotation cleanup. This makes all of those jobs run 10x more often on every instance, unrelated to the annotation deadlock fix and with potentially significant DB/IO load. It may also increase the frequency of the annotation cleanup that is reported to deadlock. Revert this change or make the interval configurable and justify it separately.

findings.title: Normal cleanup progress is logged at Error level, including full ID lists
findings.body: The new batch-cleanup code logs every batch at error level, including the complete list of IDs and the SQL condition (lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, 579). These calls happen on every cleanup cycle and every batch, even when there is nothing to delete. With cleanup scheduled every minute and a configurable batch size that can be as large as 32767 in the tests, this can emit very large error-level log entries in normal operation and make real errors hard to spot. Use debug/info for normal progress, and avoid logging unbounded ID lists.

findings.title: MaxCount cleanup can delete beyond the configured retention count under concurrent deletes
findings.body: In the MaxCount branch, the IDs to delete are selected with LIMIT/OFFSET in one statement and deleted by ID in a separate, non-transactional statement. If annotations among the newest cfg.MaxCount rows are deleted between the SELECT and DELETE (for example by a user deleting an annotation or by another cleanup process), the OFFSET window shifts. IDs that were outside the protected set at SELECT time can then be inside the newest MaxCount rows, but the DELETE still removes them, leaving fewer than MaxCount annotations and losing data beyond the configured retention policy. The previous DELETE-with-subquery made the selection and deletion atomic for this purpose. Revalidate the offset in the DELETE or otherwise make the two steps atomic/guarded.
